_comment: Feature 006 — the committed source of the in-app client changelog. Ingested at agent boot and via POST /admin/content/reingest. Each entry upserts by `slug` (idempotent). Client-facing register: keep it tester-friendly, no dev detail. A live Admin -> Updates edit of the same slug wins over this file.

entries.title: Choose your vault
entries.body: You can now pick which vault to use on the Vault page — starting with our conservative launch vault plus a hand-picked option that routes to Morpho. Your choice carries through to deposit and withdraw. Two things never change: before any deposit, the app checks the vault is one we've verified (you'll see a ✓), and you can always withdraw your funds yourself, no matter what. Where a vault's yield rate isn't measured yet, we show a dash rather than a made-up number. (The second option is currently a testnet demo vault.)

entries.title: Fair limits for the AI assistant
entries.body: The AI assistant now has fair daily limits, so it stays fast and available for everyone. The free tier is generous and fully capable — your vault, deposits, swaps, and withdraw-anytime are never affected by a limit. If you reach the day's free limit, the assistant simply tells you, and it resets the next day. You can see how much you've used on the Premium page; Premium members get higher limits, priority when things are busy, and a smarter, faster AI model.

entries.title: Real token and network icons
entries.body: The Swap page and the network switcher now show real token logos (ETH, USDC, and more) and network logos, instead of just a symbol and a colored dot. A token without a known logo — like a brand-new or testnet token — falls back to a clean lettered badge. The icon is only for recognition: whether a token is verified is still shown separately, so a look-alike logo can never vouch for a token.

entries.title: Swap into any token — not just ETH and USDC
entries.body: The Swap page now works like a full DEX. Keep ETH and USDC as one-tap picks, or paste any token's contract address to swap into it. SparkPoint reads the token straight from the chain, finds the best route automatically — routing through WETH or USDC when there's no direct pool — and always shows whether a token is verified, asking you to confirm before you receive an unverified one. You still sign every swap from your own wallet; SparkPoint never holds your funds.

entries.title: Switching wallets is recognized right away
entries.body: If you switch to a different wallet in your browser extension — anywhere in the app — SparkPoint now picks up the new wallet immediately and asks you to sign in for it, instead of getting stuck on the previous wallet's access status. Your funds are never affected; withdrawals and exit stay open no matter what.

entries.title: SparkPoint keeps itself up to date
entries.body: When we ship an update, SparkPoint now quietly refreshes to the newest version and shows you what changed — including a quick welcome the first time you drop in — and it always waits until any transaction or unsaved work is safely finished first.

entries.title: Wallet holdings on every network
entries.body: Your Portfolio now lists your native ETH plus every token your wallet holds — on Base, Base Sepolia, and Robinhood testnet.

entries.title: Sparky has a consistent voice
entries.body: The assistant now speaks with one on-brand character — clearer and steadier, and still no hype or emoji.

entries.title: A live What's New feed
entries.body: Open the changelog any time from the left rail to see everything we've shipped to the alpha.

entries.title: Steadier chat
entries.body: Chat now recovers from brief gateway hiccups instead of failing a turn — fewer "hit a problem" messages.
